# Phase 4 source fixtures

`scripts/build_phase4_fixtures.py` executes selected immutable Windows 0.11.3 Python AST definitions and writes deterministic `testdata/phase4/fixtures/contracts.json`. No reference files are modified.

Run with `python3 -B scripts/build_phase4_fixtures.py`, then `python3 -B scripts/build_phase4_fixtures.py --check`. Check mode compares bytes and does not overwrite. It uses only stdlib Python and temporary JSONL under this workspace. No network, external tool, package install, or legacy test is invoked.

Expected values come from executing AST-extracted definitions. Inputs are scripted and source functions stay intact except for the explicitly listed boundaries: `PassiveSourceClient.get_json` returns scripted provider payloads/errors and records arguments; provider-plan result callables are inert while `_provider_plan` executes; DNS `resolve_host` executes with scripted `query_rr`; `WildcardAnalyzer.analyze_parent` executes with ordinal-scripted `HostResolution` values carrying actual `RRQuery` A signatures. `secrets.token_hex`, timestamps and UUIDs are deterministic. For DNS event fixtures, source `Event`, `_relation`, `_emit_resolution_records` and `_validation_event` execute. `append_event` and `DNSRunIndex` are minimal capture sinks; `ScopeChecker` returns `in_scope` for these authorized fixture names. Provider `iter_jsonl` reads only the generated local JSONL file. Domain normalization is an ASCII-only stand-in; full PSL/Unicode behavior belongs to phase 1. Source hashes and Linux parity are recorded.

`contracts.json` has flat `inputs`/`outputs` groups for passive providers/planning, DNS resolution/wildcard/inventory, and `dns.events` cases: root terminal IP, non-root CNAME plus terminal IP, and resolvable name with uncertain wildcard parent. Event IDs and timestamps are omitted from event outputs because they are generated identifiers/time fields; every other Event field is retained. Event fixtures preserve event type, source tool, confidence, scope, metadata, structured resolution/signature, validation records, and relationship endpoints/types/evidence.

Limitations: no asynchronous resolver/provider transport, live responses, native tools, provider cap-incomplete policy, or Go implementation output is used as an oracle.

`passive.health` executes actual source `EventType`, `ScopeStatus`, `ProviderObservation`, `ProviderResult` and `_health_event` definitions with scripted result values and a capture sink. Its four cases cover complete CT, partial THC, an unavailable provider and stale-cache fallback. All stable event fields are retained; only Event ID and outer timestamps are omitted. `_health_event` does not emit anomaly status; that assessment belongs to the separate completeness/report path. There are 17 output groups; the prior 16 input/output groups are unchanged by this extension.

`passive.completeness` is group 18. It executes actual `evidence/completeness.py` constants, `AnomalyAssessment`, classification/anomaly/unique-contribution helpers and `build_run_artifact` with source `ProviderResult` and inline historical rows. Four cases cover no history, partial collection, an output collapse and invalid completeness-state normalization. History supplies diagnostic context only; historical hostnames are asserted absent from output. No directory history discovery is substituted for the production reader here; that boundary is tested separately with local fixtures. The source artifact filename is `passive_provider_completeness.json`; all stable fields, including the legacy `academic_purpose` explanation of result trust, are retained. The builder emits no generated timestamp. No academic comparison metrics are added; the prior 17 input/output groups are unchanged.
